summary: The article recounts how the Houston Astros used a center-field camera, a live feed and trash-can banging to steal opposing teams' signs in 2017 and early 2018. It covers MLB's investigation and punishments, why the World Series title and players were not penalized, fan backlash, and rule changes like PitchCom. The Astros remain stigmatized despite continued postseason success.
one_line: Explains how the 2017 Houston Astros used cameras and trash-can banging to steal signs, MLB's limited punishment, and the aftermath.
key_facts: Jim Crane obtained Astros club ownership on Nov. 17, 2011, and hired Jeff Luhnow, a former McKinsey & Company consultant, as General Manager that year.
In 2014, Crane brought in A.J. Hinch as manager after the firing of Bo Porter.
The Astros stole signs throughout the 2017 season and the beginning of 2018, until Ken Rosenthal and Evan Drellich of The Athletic reported on it the following year.
The Astros installed a camera in center field at Minute Maid Park to record opposing catchers' and pitchers' signs, with a live feed viewable behind the scenes.
Then-bench coach Alex Cora had a screen installed in the dugout; players banged on trash cans, often with bats, with different rhythms signaling different pitches.
MLB investigated 68 people, including 23 Astros players, and collected more than 76,000 emails, according to The Athletic.
On Jan. 13, 2020, MLB suspended Luhnow and Hinch for the 2020 season, and Jim Crane fired both a few hours later.
MLB fined the Astros $5 million, the maximum amount, and made them forfeit first and second-round draft picks.
Commissioner Robert Manfred refused to strip the 2017 World Series title, calling it 'difficult and impractical' and later calling the trophy a 'piece of metal,' for which he apologized.
Players were granted full immunity in exchange for cooperating with the investigation.
Jose Altuve, Alex Bregman, Lance McCullers Jr., and Justin Verlander are the four players from the original team still in Houston.
Fans at Dodgers games threw inflatable trash cans onto the field after the Astros beat the Dodgers in the 2017 World Series.
MLB restricted video replay from including the catcher's signs in 2020 and introduced PitchCom devices in 2022.
The Astros are in their seventh straight postseason.
